data.one_liner: Flutter plugin for authenticating users with a web service using OAuth or custom redirect schemes.
data.what_it_does: Allows your app to open an authentication web flow (using system browser tabs or web views) and capture the result when it redirects back via a custom URL scheme or universal link. Supports iOS, Android, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
use_when: You need to authenticate users with OAuth2 providers like Google, Facebook, or custom web services.
You need to capture custom URI schemes or universal links resulting from a web authentication flow.
avoid_when: You prefer an all-in-one backend SDK that manages state and persistent sessions out-of-the-box.
Your callback URL scheme does not conform to RFC 3986 requirements.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including mobile, desktop, and web.
Uses native secure APIs like ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS and Chrome Auth Tab on Android.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific configuration such as manifest activity filters and custom schemes.
Desktop platforms require careful setup of WebView dependencies or handling http://localhost redirects.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding a custom intent-filter Activity in AndroidManifest.xml and optionally configuring Universal Links on iOS and desktop webview window setups.

alternatives.name: google_sign_in
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically and exclusively need Google Sign-In rather than general OAuth flows.

alternatives.name: flutter_appauth
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a dedicated wrapper around AppAuth libraries for OAuth2 and OpenID Connect.

alternatives.name: sign_in_with_apple
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need native Sign in with Apple integration.
